name: GitHub Copilot SDK — direct to APIM
summary: Copilot SDK BYOK provider pointed straight at the APIM AI Gateway, bypassing Foundry entirely.
description: APIM already exposes an OpenAI-compatible surface, so `base_url = "https://<apim>.azure-api.net/openai/v1/"` + APIM subscription key (or a static JWT via `bearerToken`) lets the Copilot SDK talk to your AI Gateway without any Foundry involvement. In this topology there is no `{conn}/{model}` BYOM prefix — the model string is just the APIM deployment name, because you're already at the gateway.
notes:
Two invocation paths are supported (in preference order): (1) if `HOSTED_AGENT_NAME_COPILOT_CANARY` is wired, the test invokes the Copilot canary hosted agent — deployed by the `ai-gateway-pe-testing` infra repo — which runs inside the Foundry VNet and can reach APIM's private endpoint; (2) otherwise, a direct `CopilotClient` call from the runner, which only works when the runner has line-of-sight to APIM. APIM in this environment has `publicNetworkAccess=disabled` so GitHub-hosted runners return `403 public network access ... is disabled` on path (2).

Auth on the direct path uses `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key` or `bearer_token`; the canary uses the hosted agent's managed identity scoped to `https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default`. No BYOM prefix is expected in this topology because APIM is already the gateway; `wire_model` is the APIM deployment name. See `test.py`. For a companion card that exercises the Copilot SDK's built-in shell/files tools through the same route, see `copilot-sdk-builtin-tools`. Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities; sample: https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/docs/auth/byok.md.
